The polyline starts from a point on the left side of the bottom edge of the rectangle, then rises to the first peak point, descends to a valley point, rises again to the second peak point, descends to a fold point on the right side, and finally falls to a point on the right side of the bottom edge of the rectangle. There are six angles marked in gray in total: one angle at the left endpoint, the larger exterior angles are marked at the two peak points, one angle each at the valley point and the right-side fold point, and one angle at the right endpoint. Reasoning: According to the specified method, denote the six vertices of the polyline from left to right as A, B, C, D, E, F, where A and F are on the bottom edge of the rectangle. Let the directed inclination angles of the five line segments AB, BC, CD, DE, EF relative to the rightward horizontal line be x1, x2, x3, x4, x5 respectively. According to the positions of the gray angles in the figure: the angle at point A uses the leftward bottom-edge ray, so it is 180° − x1; the peak angle at point B is the larger reflex angle, so it is 180° + x1 − x2; the valley angle at point C is 180° + x2 − x3; the peak angle at point D is the larger reflex angle, so it is 180° + x3 − x4; the angle at the right-side fold point E is 180° + x4 − x5; the angle at point F uses the rightward bottom-edge ray, so it is 180° + x5.
